class.name: FellowGasVolume3D
class.brief_description: FellowEngine: smoke and fire simulated on the GPU in a box, drawn by the Forward+ renderer.
class.description: Simulates gas on a regular grid in a box (its floor centred on the node, [member size] metres, [member resolution] cells along its longest side): smoke, temperature and fuel advected by a staggered velocity field (MacCormack), fuel burning above [member ignition_temperature] into heat and soot, buoyancy, vorticity confinement, the physics bodies inside the box as obstacles, a pressure projection. [FellowGasEmitter3D] children emit smoke, fuel and heat. One step per physics tick (deterministic at a fixed tick rate). The Forward+ renderer draws the volume with self-shadowing, the sun's shadow on the scene and the fire's blackbody emission; an [OmniLight3D] the node owns lights the scene from the fire. Requires a RenderingDevice renderer. See [code]docs/decisions/0117-gas-simulation.md[/code] and [code]0118-gas-rendering.md[/code]. In the editor the simulation steps as in the running game (each step asks for a frame); the 3D editor's toolbar toggle [b]Animate[/b] (the editor setting [code]editors/3d/fellow/animate_nodes[/code]) off holds it after its [member prewarm_steps] (milestone 52).

method.name: get_cell_size
method.description: The cells' edge in metres (the longest side of [member size] over [member resolution]).

method.name: get_debug_data
method.description: The data of the last [method request_debug_data], once [method is_debug_data_ready]: the texture's texels as raw bytes (for tests).

method.name: get_fire_light_node
method.description: The [OmniLight3D] the node places at the fire (internal; [member fire_light]), or [code]null[/code].

method.name: get_fire_power
method.description: The fire's total emission at the last readback (the sum of the burning cells' brightness, 2-3 frames late): 0 when nothing burns.

method.name: get_grid_size
method.description: The grid's cells along X, Y and Z (from [member size] and [member resolution]).

method.name: get_steps_simulated
method.description: The simulation steps run since the start or the last [method reset_simulation].

method.name: get_velocity_texture
method.description: The velocity at the cell centres as a [Texture3D] with [member velocity_texture_enabled] (each component v / [member velocity_texture_scale] mapped to 0-1), for a [GPUParticlesAttractorVectorField3D] over the box.

method.name: get_vram_bytes
method.description: The video memory of the simulation's textures and buffers.

method.name: is_debug_data_ready
method.description: [code]true[/code] when the data of [method request_debug_data] has arrived.

method.name: request_debug_data
method.description: Reads a GPU state back asynchronously, for tests: [param what] 0 the scalars (smoke, temperature, fuel), 1 the velocity, 2 the pressure, 3 the divergence's right-hand side, 4 the solid cells. Poll [method is_debug_data_ready].

method.name: reset_simulation
method.description: Empties the box: no smoke, heat or fuel, the gas at rest (then [member prewarm_steps] again).

members.member: How much of the scene's ambient light the smoke scatters.
The smoke's scattering phase (Henyey-Greenstein): positive scatters forwards (bright towards the sun), negative backwards.
How hot gas rises: 1 is an ideal gas's buoyancy, 0 none, negative sinks.
How fast fuel burns where the gas is above [member ignition_temperature], per second.
The sun's shadow through the smoke on the scene (in the contact shadow mask; not with the ray-traced sun shadows).
The box's faces that are walls (by default the floor); the others are open to fresh air, or an inflow where [member wind] blows in.
The physics layers whose bodies are obstacles ([member physics_obstacles]).
How fast hot gas cools towards the ambient temperature, per second.

Draws the smoke faded out within this distance (metres) of the box's faces, all but a closed floor ([member closed_faces]), so the box does not show where the smoke leaves through an open face or piles against a wall. It changes only the drawing (and the smoke's shadows), not the simulation. 0: none.
How much burning fuel expands the gas (a source in the pressure projection): flames that push outwards.
The fire's blackbody emission's brightness (it grows with the fourth power of the temperature).
An [OmniLight3D] at the fire lights the scene, its energy and colour from the simulated emission (2-3 frames late).
A multiplier of the fire light's energy, which follows the fire's emission.
The fire light's range in metres (0: from its energy, 2-60 m).
The fire light casts shadows (an omni shadow: costly).
The flames' colour temperature: the gas's temperature times this is the blackbody's (higher is whiter).

The combustion heats no cell above this (kelvin; the fuel left burns further on), so that burning objects' fuel cannot run the gas away; 0: no limit (2200 K above the ambient where [FellowBurnable3D] objects feed the volume).
The heat a unit of fuel releases as it burns (kelvin per unit).
RGBA32F state textures instead of RGBA16F: for very hot or large volumes; twice the memory.
Fuel burns where the gas is hotter than this (kelvin).
MacCormack advection (second order, sharper detail) instead of semi-Lagrangian.
The multigrid solver's V-cycles a step ([member pressure_solver] Multigrid).

The physics bodies inside the box are obstacles the gas flows around (spheres, boxes, capsules, cylinders, world boundaries; other convex shapes as their box; at most 16); a body moved more than six cells in a step counts as teleported.
The SOR solver's sweeps a step ([member pressure_solver] SOR).
How the pressure projection is solved: multigrid V-cycles (faster to converge) or red-black SOR.

Steps simulated when the simulation starts or resets, so the fire is already burning: up to 32 a physics tick over the first frames, as many as the GPU's queue of steps takes before each frame is drawn.
Draws the volume (Forward+ and Mobile simulate it; only Forward+ draws it).
The ray march's step through the volume, in cells: larger is cheaper and coarser.
The cells along the box's longest side (the others in proportion).
How strongly the smoke shadows itself from the sun.
How dark the smoke's shadow on the scene is ([member cast_shadows]).
Off: the gas stays as it is (no steps), still drawn.
The box in metres, its floor centred on the node.
The smoke's scattering colour.
The smoke's extinction per metre at a smoke density of 1.
How fast smoke fades, per second.
A downward acceleration per unit of smoke (m/s²): heavy smoke sinks as it cools.
The smoke a unit of burning fuel leaves.
Local: the gas moves and turns with the node. World: the gas stays in the world and the (axis-aligned) box follows the node by whole cells (a carried torch).

Only the 4³-cell bricks near smoke, heat, fuel or an emitter are simulated (within [member sparse_margin] bricks; the velocity one brick further), the air beyond still: much cheaper for a fire in a large box.
How many bricks around the active ones are simulated ([member sparse]).
Simulation steps per physics tick, each a fraction of it (shorter steps for fast flows).
The simulation's speed: its time step is the physics tick times this.
A noise force (m/s²) that breaks the flow up.
The turbulence noise's size in metres.
Exports the velocity at the cell centres as a [Texture3D] ([method get_velocity_texture]) for a [GPUParticlesAttractorVectorField3D]: sparks and embers carried by the flow.
The speed that maps to the texture's full range ([member velocity_texture_enabled]).
Vorticity confinement: puts back the small swirls the grid smooths away.
The wind in metres per second: it blows in through the open faces and the gas inside relaxes towards it at [member wind_rate].
The active [FellowWind3D]'s velocity at the box, with its gusts, instead of [member wind].
How fast the gas inside the box takes the wind's velocity, per second (0: only through the open faces).

constants.constant: The gas moves and turns with the node.
The gas stays in the world; the box (axis-aligned) follows the node by whole cells.
